verses.text: Some time later, there was a man named Naboth from Jezreel who owned a vineyard in Jezreel. It was right next to the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

Ahab said to Naboth, "Give me your vineyard so I can use it for a vegetable garden, since it is close to my palace. In exchange I will give you a better vineyard. Or if you prefer, I will pay you what it is worth."
But Naboth said to Ahab, "The LORD forbid that I should give you the land I inherited from my ancestors!"

So Ahab went home sulking and angry because of what Naboth from Jezreel had said: "I will not give you the land I inherited from my ancestors." He lay on his bed, turned his face to the wall, and would not eat.
His wife Jezebel came in and asked him, "Why are you so upset that you will not eat?"
He told her, "I spoke to Naboth from Jezreel and said, 'Sell me your vineyard. Or if you like, I will give you another vineyard for it.' But he said, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"
His wife Jezebel said, "Is this how you rule as king of Israel? Get up, eat something, and cheer up. I will get you the vineyard of Naboth from Jezreel."
So she wrote letters in Ahab's name, stamped them with his seal, and sent them to the leaders and important men who lived in Naboth's town.
In the letters she wrote: "Announce a day of fasting, and give Naboth a seat of honour among the people.
Then seat two worthless men across from him, and have them accuse him, saying, 'You cursed God and the king!' Then take him out and stone him to death."
The leaders and important men of Naboth's town did just what Jezebel told them in the letters she had sent them.
They announced a fast and gave Naboth a seat of honour among the people.

Then the two worthless men came in and sat across from him. They accused Naboth in front of the people, saying, "Naboth cursed God and the king!" So they took him outside the town and stoned him to death.
Then they sent word to Jezebel: "Naboth has been stoned, and he is dead."

As soon as Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned to death, she said to Ahab, "Get up and take the vineyard of Naboth from Jezreel, the one he refused to sell you. Naboth is not alive anymore. He is dead."
When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he got up and went down to take the vineyard of Naboth from Jezreel for himself.
Then the LORD's word came to Elijah from Tishbe. He said,
"Get up and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who rules in Samaria. He is in Naboth's vineyard right now. He has gone there to take it for himself.

Tell him, 'This is what the LORD says: Have you murdered a man and also taken his land?' Then tell him, 'This is what the LORD says: In the same place where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, dogs will lick up your blood, yes, yours!'"
Ahab said to Elijah, "So you have found me, my enemy!" Elijah answered, "Yes, I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do what is evil in the LORD's eyes.
The LORD says, 'I am going to bring disaster on you. I will wipe you out and cut off every male in Ahab's family in Israel, slave or free.
I will make your family like the family of Jeroboam son of Nebat and the family of Baasha son of Ahijah, because you have made me angry and have made Israel sin.'
And about Jezebel the LORD says, 'Dogs will eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.'
Dogs will eat anyone in Ahab's family who dies in the city, and birds will eat those who die in the open country."
There was never anyone like Ahab, who sold himself to do what was evil in the LORD's eyes, urged on by his wife Jezebel.
He did disgusting things by worshipping idols, just as the Amorites had done, the people the LORD drove out ahead of the Israelites.
When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went without food. He even slept in sackcloth and walked around quietly in sorrow.
Then the LORD's word came to Elijah from Tishbe. He said,
"Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself, I will not bring the disaster while he is alive. I will bring it on his family in his son's time."
